transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to call this coverage huddle to order. As you know, the Advanced Chemistry teacher will be absent for three consecutive school days next month, and I need to approve both the coverage roster and the instructional plan before it's posted to staff. The draft plan currently on the table uses one substitute, regular classroom activities, and the standard make-up-work process. Before I make a decision, I'd like to hear from each of you — department chair, HR coordinator, nurse, and counselor — on any relevant updates that might affect this plan. Let's start with the department chair.

transcript.text: I need to flag an important issue. My department calendar shows that the class's graded chemistry lab practical is scheduled for the second day of the absence, and it cannot be replaced by a worksheet. Department policy requires a chemistry-certified teacher to supervise it. I entered the practical in the department calendar this week but had not yet forwarded the calendar note to Ms. Morgan, so this may not have been factored into the draft plan.

transcript.text: I have an important update from the HR side. transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a critical health and safety update. A student in the Advanced Chemistry class has an active seizure action plan that requires an adult trained in seizure response to remain in the classroom during laboratory activities. I confirmed both the seizure action plan and Dr. Lena Park's seizure response training record this week — her training is current — but I have not yet attached either record to the coverage request. This is directly relevant to the lab practical Mr. Singh just flagged, since the action plan specifically applies during lab activities.

I recorded the request in my counseling file but have not yet sent it to the classroom teacher, so it would not have been factored into the draft plan's standard make-up-work process.
